title: 3 Ideas at Noon: How StoryVaultFiles Works
description:
Nobody edits these videos by hand. Here is how StoryVaultFiles turns one tap into a video.

This Short walks through the pipeline: three daily story ideas on Telegram, an AI-written script, a narrated and illustrated edit, and publishing to YouTube and Instagram after a human approves.

Would you watch a video that no person edited by hand? Tell us in the comments.
look: 2026, dim modern workspace with glowing screens, phone and desk objects, cool blue and warm lamp light, documentary style

shots.text: Nobody sits at an editing desk here, yet a full video gets made.
shots.image_prompt: wide shot of an empty video editing desk with dark monitors in a quiet room, a glowing phone on the desk, cool blue light
close-up of a smartphone on a dark wooden desk showing a chat window, soft glow, shallow depth of field

shots.text: Every day at noon, Toronto time, a message arrives on Telegram.
shots.image_prompt: medium shot of a wall clock showing twelve o'clock above a city office window, Toronto skyline haze, midday light

shots.text: Three mystery cases, pulled from Wikipedia and pitched by AI.
shots.image_prompt: three old manila case folders fanned out on a desk under a green lamp, dramatic low-key lighting, close-up
close-up of a thumb pressing a phone screen in a dim room, screen glow on the fingertip

shots.text: Claude researches it and writes the script, with Gemini as the backup.
shots.image_prompt: over-the-shoulder view of a silhouetted figure at a glowing monitor full of lines of text, dark room, soft blue light

shots.text: A free neural voice records the narration.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of a vintage studio microphone with a pop filter, dark booth, warm rim light

shots.text: Then every sentence gets its own AI picture, period-accurate and photoreal.
shots.image_prompt: wide shot of a wall of black and white photographic prints pinned in a dim darkroom, red safelight, film grain

shots.text: Real people are never drawn as recognisable faces.
shots.image_prompt: silhouette of a person from behind standing before a bright window, face unseen, dusty light beams

shots.text: If the daily picture allowance runs out, stock footage fills in.
shots.image_prompt: medium shot of a film archive shelf with labelled reels in metal canisters, dusty, low light

shots.text: FFmpeg cuts it all together into a long video and a vertical Short.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of a film editor's hands cutting a strip of film on a splicing table, warm lamp, tight framing

shots.text: The preview lands back on Telegram.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of a phone propped against a coffee cup showing a paused video, morning light on a table

shots.text: Don't like the intro? Type a note, and it rewrites and re-renders.
shots.image_prompt: medium shot of hands typing on a phone beside a handwritten page covered in crossed-out lines, desk lamp
extreme close-up of a finger hovering over a glowing phone screen button, dark background, shallow focus

shots.text: The video and Short go to YouTube, and the Short goes to Instagram.
shots.image_prompt: wide shot of a laptop and a phone side by side on a desk, both showing glowing video players, night room

shots.text: Every upload waits for a human's approval.
shots.image_prompt: medium shot of a hand holding a rubber stamp above a stack of papers, desk lamp, moody light

shots.text: The whole thing runs on free tiers.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of a worn jar of coins on a windowsill, soft daylight, muted tones
